explanation: Use an unsigned rolling polynomial hash for the pattern and each equal-length text window. A matching hash triggers a full character comparison, so hash collisions cannot produce a false match. Return the first verified window.
timeComplexity: O(n + m) time when hash matches are rare; O(nm) worst-case time with repeated hash collisions, for text length n and pattern length m.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: The rolling hash invariant is the polynomial hash of the current text window, using unsigned wraparound arithmetic consistently for pattern and text. Removing the outgoing weighted character, multiplying by the radix and adding the incoming character preserves that invariant. Equal hashes trigger an exact span comparison, so collisions cannot create false matches. Windows are considered from left to right, making the first verified match the required answer.
walkthrough: Search text cedar-ridge for pattern ridge. The pattern has length 5. The initial window is cedar; rolling updates examine windows starting at 1 through 5 without a verified match. The window beginning at index 6 is ridge. Its hash agrees and the character comparison succeeds, so return 6.
edgeCases: An empty pattern matches at index 0.
A pattern longer than the text cannot match.
Repeated matches return the first index; equal hashes alone never establish equality.
